sentences.text: 1. The sister of appellant No.1 filed a suit for partition and separate possession claiming 1/2 share in the suit schedule properties on the premise that the suit schedule properties are inherited by her after the demise of her father, who died in the year 1982 and the demise of the mother, who died in the year 1990.

2. Defendant No.2 is the son of defendant No.1 and he is added as a party to the proceedings on the premise that the Gift Deed executed by defendant No.1 in favour of his son is not binding on the share of the plaintiff, as the plaintiff's consent is not obtained.

Defendant No.3 is impleaded as a party on the premise that he purchased the property without the consent of the plaintiff and the defendant No.4 - the Special Land Acquisition Officer, Karnataka Industrial Area Development Board, is added on the NC: 2023:KHC-D:10832 premise that plaintiff is not heard before acquiring the property and determining the compensation.

entities.text: Special Land Acquisition Officer, Karnataka Industrial Area Development Board
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text:
3. Defendants No.1 and 2 contested the case on the premise that the daughter is born before 1956, as such, she is not entitled to share in the properties and defendant No.3 contested the suit on the premise that he is the bona fide purchaser of 2 acres of the property in the said land.
4. The suit is decreed holding that the plaintiff is entitled to 1/2 share in item No.1 of suit 'B'
schedule properties and 1/2 share in item No.2 of suit 'B' schedule properties.
Since Item No.1 property is said to have been acquired and the compensation is awarded, the trial Court has declared 1/2 share in item No.1 of the compensation amount.
Defendants Nos.1 and 2 are in appeal.

5. Sri.Gode Nagaraja, learned counsel appearing on behalf of appellants submits that, the trial Court NC: 2023:KHC-D:10832 ignored the fact the plaintiff was born before 1956 and as such, she cannot claim equal share in the properties.
It is also his contention that the suit is filed 28 years after the death of the father.
The suit is barred by limitation.
6. This Court has considered the contentions raised at the Bar.

The following points arise for consideration:
i. Whether the daughter born before 1956 is not entitled for the share in the properties left behind by the father?
ii.
Whether the suit for partition filed 28 years after the death of the father is barred by limitation?
7. Admittedly, in this case the properties are acquired by the father Kolkar Basappa who died in the year 1982.
The properties would devolve under Section 8 of the Hindu Succession Act 1956, on his Class-I heirs namely wife Hanumakka, son Kolkar Timmappa and daughter Shivamma.
Hanumakka acquire 1/3rd share, Kolkar Timmappa acquire 1/3rd share and NC: 2023:KHC-D:10832 Shivappa acquire 1/3rd share.
Hanumakka died on 15.08.1990 and her share devolves on her son Kolkar Timmappa and her daughter Shivamma as Hanumakka died intestate.
Thus, Kolkar Timmappa acquired 1/2 share and Shivamma acquired 1/2 share.
The suit is filed in the year 2008.

Kolkar Thimmappa vs Smt.Shivamma on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97469054/
3 8.

The contention that the plaintiff is not entitled to claim share in the properties as she was born before 1956 is untenable for the simple reason, after the death of the father, his self-acquired properties devolve on Class-I heirs of propositus Kolkar Basappa.
The date of birth of the daughter is immaterial.
Since the daughter is Class-I heir she is entitled to inherit the properties of the father.
9. In a suit for partition to hold that the suit is barred by limitation the defendants must establish the ouster.
No such plea of ouster is found in the pleadings.
The evidence also does not support the contention on limitation.

Under the circumstances, the trial Court has rightly held that the plaintiff is entitled to share in the compensation amount in respect of item No.1 of 'B' schedule properties and 1/2 share in item No.2 of 'B' schedule properties.
11. As far as the contention of defendant No.3 that he is the bona fide purchaser of the property, it to be noticed that the suit is one for partition.
No evidence is placed to the effect that the plaintiff consented for the sale.
The plaintiff is not a signatory to the sale deed executed by defendant No.1.
Defendant No.3 has failed to establish his defence.
12. As far as Gift Deed in favour of defendant No.2 is concerned, same is invalid as the plaintiff who is the co-sharer did not consent for the gift.
The Gift Deed doesn't bind the right of the plaintiff.
13. This Court has perused the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court.
The trial Court has NC: 2023:KHC-D:10832 assigned valid reasons to grant a decree.

For the aforementioned reasons,
this Court does not find any merit in the appeal.
14. After the disposal of the suit, the defendant filed an petition to review the judgment.
The petition is filed on the premise that the plaintiff is not entitled to equal share in the suit property.
The said petition was registered as Misc.No.1/2016.
The trial Court dismissed the petition on the premise that subsequent change in the interpretation of law cannot be a ground for review.

Thus, the appellant has also questioned the order dated 18.04.2016 dismissing the Misc.No.1/2016.
15.

As this Court has already noticed the plaintiff inherited the property under Section 8 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, the defendant cannot seek review of the order on the premise that interpretation of Section 6 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 has changed.
Thus, there is no merit in NC: 2023:KHC-D:10832 the challenge to the order dismissing the review petition.
16. Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed.
The judgment and decree dated 29.10.2015 passed by the I Addl.
Senior Civil Judge, Ballari, in O.S.No.46/2008 and the order dated 18.04.2016 passed by the I Addl.
Senior Civil Judge, Ballari, in Misc.No.1/2016, are confirmed.
No order as to cost.
